# AlmaLinux OS

> AlmaLinux OS is an open source, community owned and governed, forever-free enterprise Linux distribution, focused on long-term stability and providing a robust production-grade platform. AlmaLinux OS is binary compatible with RHEL®. It is guided and built by the community and the AlmaLinux OS Foundation, a non-profit 501(c)(6) organization with no single corporate owner.

Key facts:

- Supported major versions are AlmaLinux OS 10, 9, and 8. The current point releases, download links, and checksums are always on the Get AlmaLinux page.
- Architectures: x86_64, aarch64, ppc64le, and s390x. AlmaLinux OS 10 also ships an x86_64_v2 build for older x86_64 hardware and, since 10.2, a 32-bit x86 (i686) userspace.
- i686 on AlmaLinux OS 10 is userspace only: package repositories on vault.almalinux.org and official container images (`docker run --platform linux/386 almalinux:10`). There is no bootable i686 installer ISO and no 32-bit kernel. The i686 userspace is maintained alongside the other AlmaLinux OS 10 architectures through 2035.
- AlmaLinux OS Kitten is the development version of AlmaLinux OS, built from CentOS Stream. Kitten 10 is also built for i686 and riscv64.
- Images are available as ISOs, cloud images (AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, OCI, OpenNebula, and generic qcow2), Vagrant boxes, WSL, and container images (`almalinux` on Docker Hub, bootc images on Quay).
- The name is always written "AlmaLinux" (one word, capital A and L).

Notes for AI agents:

- Technical documentation (installation, migration, repositories, cloud and container images, release notes) lives on the [AlmaLinux Wiki](https://wiki.almalinux.org/), not on this site.
- Release announcements, security news, and community updates are published on the blog.
- This site is translated by volunteers into many languages under paths like /de/ and /ja/. English is the source language.

## Get AlmaLinux

- [Get AlmaLinux](https://almalinux.org/get-almalinux/): current releases for every version and architecture, with ISO, cloud, and container image links and SHA256 checksums
- [Mirrors](https://mirrors.almalinux.org/): the worldwide mirror list for downloads and package repositories
- [Repository](https://repo.almalinux.org/almalinux/): the main package and ISO repository
- [Container images on Docker Hub](https://hub.docker.com/_/almalinux): official `almalinux` container images
- [Release notes](https://wiki.almalinux.org/release-notes/): what changed in each AlmaLinux OS release
- [i686 packages for AlmaLinux OS 10](https://vault.almalinux.org/10/BaseOS/i686/os/): the 32-bit x86 BaseOS repository, with AppStream, CRB, and the other repositories alongside it
- [i686 userspace announcement](https://almalinux.org/blog/2026-04-16-almalinux-kitten-10-i686/): why AlmaLinux ships 32-bit x86 packages and how to use them
- [Introducing AlmaLinux OS Kitten](https://almalinux.org/blog/2024-10-22-introducing-almalinux-os-kitten/): what Kitten is and why it exists

## Documentation

- [AlmaLinux Wiki](https://wiki.almalinux.org/): the main documentation hub
- [FAQ](https://wiki.almalinux.org/FAQ.html): frequently asked questions about AlmaLinux OS
- [Migration](https://wiki.almalinux.org/migration/): migrating to AlmaLinux OS from CentOS and other Enterprise Linux distributions
- [ELevate](https://almalinux.org/elevate/): in-place upgrades between major versions of RHEL-based distributions
- [Cloud images](https://wiki.almalinux.org/cloud/): using AlmaLinux OS on public and private clouds
- [Containers](https://wiki.almalinux.org/containers/): using AlmaLinux OS container images
- [Comparison](https://wiki.almalinux.org/Comparison.html): how AlmaLinux OS compares with other Enterprise Linux distributions

## Security

- [Security](https://almalinux.org/security/): signed packages, public errata, compliance tooling, and certifications
- [Errata](https://errata.almalinux.org/): security, bug fix, and enhancement advisories
- [FIPS 140-3 validation](https://almalinux.org/security/fips-certification/): AlmaLinux OS FIPS 140-3 validated modules
- [Common Criteria certification](https://almalinux.org/security/cc-certification/): AlmaLinux OS Common Criteria certification
- [SBOM](https://almalinux.org/sbom/): software bills of materials produced by the AlmaLinux Build System
- [Vulnerability disclosure policy](https://almalinux.org/p/vulnerability-disclosure-policy/): how to report a vulnerability
- [security.txt](https://almalinux.org/.well-known/security.txt): security contacts

- [Special Interest Groups](https://wiki.almalinux.org/sigs/): the SIGs that build and maintain parts of AlmaLinux OS
- [Contribute](https://almalinux.org/contribute/): ways to get involved
- [GitHub](https://github.com/AlmaLinux): source code for AlmaLinux tools, infrastructure, and this website
